answer.rationale: Rated against the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not against internal plausibility. A general caveat applies to all six: every entry is a consolidated summary with the source archived, so none carries effect size, sample size, confidence interval, observation window, or segment definition. That ceiling means nothing here earns a 5. memory_57 scores highest (4) because it is the only entry whose stated outcome is denominated in the target currency — 'qualified revenue' — and the only one that explicitly checks a durability guardrail (no measurable harm to retention); its weakness is that 'no measurable harm' may reflect low power rather than true null, and it says nothing about referral supply exhausting. memory_44 (3) speaks to pipeline quality, which is one step from qualified revenue, but pipeline quality is not closed-won revenue and no conversion or cycle-length data is given; it is also about enterprise, a segment orthogonal to the current SMB pressure. memory_73 (2) claims revenue lift, but promotional pricing is exactly the intervention where short-window revenue and long-term revenue diverge: the memory omits margin, discount-cohort retention, renewal price realization, and whether the lift persisted past the promo period — and a competitor price war is the scenario where those omissions matter most. memory_31 (2) and memory_86 (2) both report activation/completion/time-to-value proxies with no link to revenue or retention; 'durable' in memory_31 is asserted rather than quantified, and improved completion could reflect a shorter funnel measuring less rather than better-qualified accounts. memory_91 is least supported (1): week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the furthest-upstream proxies in the set, 'nudged more accounts' is directionally vague, and there is no bridge at all to retention, expansion, or revenue — it is the weakest evidentiary basis for a revenue objective even though the current activation dip makes it superficially topical. Note the general pattern: the memories that feel most relevant to today's symptoms (activation down, onboarding down, competitor pricing) are precisely the ones with the weakest revenue linkage, so symptom-matching should not drive the single experiment slot.
